left_out: the notes don't explain it: The notes do not explain what 'Moab is My washbasin' means. Calvin only gives the verse (as 'the pot of my washing') and points back to Psalm 60. Matthew Henry says only that David looks on Moab, Edom and Philistia as already his, because God promised him victory over his enemies. He says nothing about a washbasin. Clarke and Gill add nothing about this phrase. The idea of a menial servant people in the idiom list is not supported by the notes.
